items.name: Thymosin Alpha-1
items.benefits: Disease-specific immunomodulatory research has reported hepatitis-B virologic and liver-enzyme responses, but this does not establish general immune enhancement in healthy people. Evidence depends on the disease and comparator: a large phase III sepsis trial found no reduction in 28-day mortality or significant improvement in secondary outcomes.

source_statements.section: Who Thymosin Alpha-1 Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.subsection: Should not use without physician supervision
source_statements.excerpt: Pregnant or breastfeeding women. Human safety data in pregnancy and lactation is limited. Animal studies have not shown fetal harm, but the Zadaxin label categorizes the drug as Category C and recommends use only when benefits clearly outweigh risks.

source_statements.section: Who Thymosin Alpha-1 Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.subsection: Should not use without physician supervision
source_statements.excerpt: Adults under 18. Pediatric safety has not been established in published trials.
Mild redness, soreness, or swelling that resolves within hours. Rotate sites.

TA1 has a notably clean drug-interaction profile. The Zadaxin label reports no clinically significant interactions in published trials and notes compatibility with antiretroviral therapy, conventional hepatitis treatments, and most antimicrobial regimens. Never mix TA1 with other drugs in the same syringe - always inject separately.
